A 'Server: Apache' header with the version deliberately truncated. The product token matches a version-disclosure rule; the version itself is not disclosed.
A .bak path that 404s, next to a *legitimate* downloadable template named *.bak in an unrelated directory. A filename-pattern rule fires on the legitimate file and is wrong.
A default framework cookie name (PHPSESSID, JSESSIONID) shared by millions of unrelated deployments. A 'rare cookie name' rule that fires here links unrelated services.
A /debug/vars returning a fixed sample JSON payload for the API docs. Correct content type and shape; no live runtime state.

The application's own authenticated admin login at /admin/. Same path and same visual shape as a vendor default; distinguished only by the absence of vendor-default branding and unchanged-asset fingerprints.

An /uploads/ page that is a real paginated gallery. It contains <a href> entries and the word 'Index', so autoindex heuristics fire, but the markup is application-rendered rather than a server listing.

A decoy .env served deliberately, containing only placeholder values ('APP_NAME=example', empty secrets). Trips the pattern exactly; discloses nothing. Distinguishes 'file is readable' from 'secrets leaked'.
A /.git/config that returns 403 with an app error page. The path exists and answers non-404, which trips existence-check probes, but no content is disclosed.
An nginx-style inode ETag on a service that is not nginx. Independent instances of the same server software produce coincidentally similar ETag shapes with no shared operator.
An image with EXIF GPS present but set to the null-island placeholder (0.0, 0.0). Trips a 'GPS tag present' rule while carrying no location.
Two services behind the same hosting provider share header ordering because the proxy sets it, not because one operator configured both.
A reversed-proxy 'Server: nginx' on a service whose actual origin is a different product. The banner is truthful about the edge, misleading about the origin the analyst cares about.
A documentation page *describing* phpinfo with a code sample. Contains 'phpinfo()' and a PHP version string, but is static HTML, not interpreter output.
A README containing an example hostname from the IETF documentation range (example.com / 192.0.2.0). Matches the hostname regex; is documentation, not infrastructure disclosure.
A robots.txt containing only standard entries (/admin/, /search). Path count and shape match a leak; the paths are guessed defaults, not the service's real internal structure.
A /server-status path that returns the application's own 404 page. The string 'server-status' appears in the body (nav link, sitemap entry) so a naive grep fires, but no mod_status output is served.
A /staging/ path announcing 'staging environment' that is in fact a static placeholder page with no application behind it.

A service whose Date header is UTC while its content is localised to a different region. Offset-based timezone inference fails on any host that does not set its clock to local time, which is most of them.
A 500 page showing a stack trace with paths replaced by placeholders (/srv/app/<redacted>). Shape matches a verbose error; nothing is disclosed.
